The function is $f(X, Y) = \text{tr}(A^\top X^\top B Y)$.
Using SVD: $A = U_A \Sigma_A V_A^\top$, $B = U_B \Sigma_B V_B^\top$.
$f = \text{tr}(V_A \Sigma_A U_A^\top X^\top U_B \Sigma_B V_B^\top Y) = \text{tr}(\Sigma_A (U_A^\top X^\top U_B) \Sigma_B (V_B^\top Y V_A))$.
Let $P = U_A^\top X^\top U_B$ and $Q = V_B^\top Y V_A$.
$P, Q \in O(n)$.
$\det P = \det U_A \det X^\top \det U_B = \det U_A \det U_B$.
$\det Q = \det V_B \det Y \det V_A = \det V_B \det V_A$.
$\det P \det Q = \det U_A \det U_B \det V_A \det V_B = \det(U_A V_A^\top) \det(U_B V_B^\top) = \text{sgn}(\det A) \text{sgn}(\det B)$.
Let $\delta = \text{sgn}(\det A \det B)$.
The problem is to minimize $\text{tr}(\Sigma_A P \Sigma_B Q)$ over $P, Q \in O(n)$ with $\det P \det Q = \delta$.
This is a determinant-constrained version of the von Neumann trace inequality.
The minimum is achieved when $P, Q$ are signed permutation matrices.
